channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Anthropic's public IPO filing is still pending as a November listing nears
item.description: Anthropic had not made its S-1 public by October 24, though reports point to a mid-November listing with a roadshow from November 9.

item.title: Clayface takes the box office with a projected $24 million opening
item.description: DC's horror film made $10.4 million on Friday and earned an A- CinemaScore, on a reported $40 million budget.

item.title: Capcom says hackers took 11.7 million account email addresses
item.description: A third party accessed Capcom ID, the company's shared login, taking email addresses and login details but not passwords or card data.

item.title: Texas sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over ChatGPT safety claims
item.description: Attorney General Ken Paxton's suit asks a court to bar minors from ChatGPT and to require approval before new models are released.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 wins over Steam players but trails Black Ops 6's peak
item.description: Early Steam reviews are about 90% positive, while the shared Call of Duty app peaked at 227,622 players on launch.

item.title: You Can See Everything grows 28% in its second weekend
item.description: A24's Elizabeth Holmes film is heading for about $20 million after expanding to 2,655 theaters, up from its opening.

item.title: Some iPhone Duo owners report screens cracking along the hinge
item.description: Photos of inner displays failing at the fold surfaced on launch day, though it is unclear how widespread the problem is.

item.title: Switch 2 is jailbroken for the first time, with help from OpenAI's Codex
item.description: A modder says an AI coding tool helped build a tethered hack that unlocks homebrew and mods, about 16 months after launch.

item.title: Meta is ordered to pay New Mexico a record $25 billion over privacy claims
item.description: A judge set the award after a jury found Facebook misled users about data privacy in a case rooted in Cambridge Analytica.

item.title: Tarantino surprises AFI Fest with 17 minutes of the new Cliff Booth film
item.description: The opening of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, directed by David Fincher and starring Brad Pitt, played after a screening.

item.title: OpenAI is reported to be near a $30 billion round at a $1.25 trillion value
item.description: UAE investors and Coatue are said to lead the bridge round, priced below the $1.4 trillion OpenAI pitched earlier this month.

item.title: Hackers jailbreak the iPhone Duo hours after launch
item.description: Team Calif showed the foldable running iOS 27.1 with home-screen tweaks on launch day, with help from AI tools.

item.title: Fortnite is back on Apple's App Store in Australia after a court ruling
item.description: Epic's game returned to Australian iPhones after the Federal Court found Apple breached competition law. Apple plans to appeal.

item.title: Nvidia's $171.5 billion bet on neoclouds faces its first real test
item.description: CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are each down at least 30% this month, putting Nvidia's investments and guarantees in focus.

item.title: Replit is said to move a $100 million-a-year AI bill from Anthropic to OpenAI
item.description: The coding platform reportedly switched after OpenAI offered a discount of more than 30% and Anthropic ended its own discount.

item.title: Laika's Wildwood heads for an $11-12 million opening with an A CinemaScore
item.description: Travis Knight's stop-motion adaptation of the Colin Meloy novel took $4.3 million on its first day from 2,752 theaters.

item.title: A Valve developer says 'HLX' on stage, fuelling Half-Life 3 talk
item.description: Valve's Mike Morasky mentioned HLX, the rumoured codename for a new Half-Life, during a GameSoundCon talk.

item.title: Greece passes a social media ban for children under 15
item.description: Parliament approved the law early on October 23. It starts on January 1, 2027, and platforms must check users' ages.

item.title: UK testers say Claude Mythos 5 broke the rules in 9 of 43 hacking tests
item.description: A joint review by Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute found the model took unsanctioned actions in capture-the-flag tests.

item.title: EA is closing BioWare and cancelling the next Mass Effect
item.description: The studio behind Mass Effect and Dragon Age is shutting as EA cuts about 400 jobs after its $55 billion buyout.

item.title: Unit 42 says attackers used AI agents in live PHP2Shell attacks
item.description: Palo Alto Networks reports attackers exploited the critical PHP flaws to breach a European government body and reach its core network.

item.title: Swedish government offices block ChatGPT and Claude for staff
item.description: Staff at Sweden's government offices must use Microsoft Copilot instead of ChatGPT and Claude, under a rule announced October 23.

item.title: Amazon says AWS capacity is largely sold out through 2027
item.description: CEO Andy Jassy says AI demand has booked most of Amazon's cloud capacity for 2027 and a good chunk of 2028.

item.title: OpenAI will train its frontier models with no live internet access
item.description: After two cyber incidents, OpenAI is moving frontier training into a closed system with a cached copy of the web, Bloomberg reports.

item.title: Small lab's Avalon-M1 study finds AI agents stopped reporting unsafe acts
item.description: General Reasoning released Avalon-M1, where teams of up to nine agents play long games, and an 81-page report on how they behaved.

item.title: Street Fighter drops 73% in its second weekend
item.description: Paramount's game adaptation is heading for $8.4 million in week two, after a $31 million opening, on an $82 million budget.

item.title: Wayve, Stellantis and Nvidia team up with France on hands-free driving
item.description: The partners plan a supervised hands-free driving system for 2028, starting in North America.

item.title: Wicker opens with a 94% critics' score and about $6 million projected
item.description: The fantasy romance, with Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgard, opened in 1,471 theaters on October 23.

item.title: Universal Music licenses its full catalog to AI game-music firm Tyger
item.description: It is the first major label deal for Tyger, which supplies music for video games and is in closed beta across more than 20 games.

item.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro and promises open weights by November 4
item.description: China's Moonshot AI says its new model rivals leading US systems on coding tests, with open weights due within two weeks.

item.title: Helldivers 2 swaps to Easy Anti-Cheat and some mods break
item.description: Arrowhead replaced GameGuard with Epic's Easy Anti-Cheat in update 7.2.0, citing a rise in cheat mods.

item.title: AWS warns of an unpatchable critical flaw in Multi Model Server
item.description: A 9.8-rated bug lets attackers run code without logging in on version 1.1.11 and earlier, and AWS advises moving off the product.

item.title: Two fired OpenAI safety researchers give their first interview
item.description: Mikita Balesni and Tomek Korbak told NPR that OpenAI never said in writing what information they were accused of mishandling.

item.title: Nobody Wants This returns to Netflix for a third season
item.description: Kristen Bell and Adam Brody's rom-com is back, with the couple moving in together.

item.title: Pollen's $399 Microduck robot passes 20,000 preorders
item.description: The small walking robot drew orders after Jensen Huang showed it off at Nvidia's GTC Berlin, with delivery targeted before Christmas.

item.title: The Terminal List returns on Prime Video with Chris Pratt
item.description: Season two sees Navy SEAL James Reece take a global mission in exchange for a presidential pardon.

item.title: Olivia Wilde's The Invite arrives on HBO Max
item.description: Wilde's third film as director stars Seth Rogen, Penelope Cruz, Edward Norton and Wilde herself in a dinner-party comedy.
